subject: Clarify infra tolerances & isolation expectations for ClearPath POC
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@clearpathhealth.com>, Patricia Miller <pmiller@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Clarify infra tolerances & isolation expectations for ClearPath POC

Alex / Patricia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a POC that matches ClearPath's risk profile. I pulled together the SLO matrix and the requirements doc (attached).

Call recap (high level):
- Business need: embed clinical summarization + triage in the clinician workflow. Latency is critical for provider adoption; long tail spikes kill UX.
- Current volume estimate: ~300 requests/min average (5 RPS), with daily peaks up to ~1,000 requests/min during mornings. Typical request size ~180–260 tokens.
- Security: some payloads will contain PHI; ClearPath requires tenant isolation and auditability.

Key questions we discussed — please confirm:
1) Latency tolerances: you mentioned p95 < 250ms as the target. Is that a hard SLA requirement for GA or a target we should aim for in POC? What is acceptable p99 during short bursts?
2) Isolation/PHI handling: do you require strict single-tenant (no co-mingling) for production, or is a Dedicated capacity pool with tenant-level segmentation acceptable?
3) Failover behavior: if Dedicated capacity hits full utilization, are you comfortable with automatic fallback to Redwood Hosted (lower-cost shared infra) with rate-limited traffic, or must requests be rejected instead?
4) Procurement/timeline: Patricia, can you confirm procurement lead time for Dedicated vs Private install? Any constraints around vendor onboarding (PO, DSAR, security questionnaire timeline)?

What we propose for a conservative POC (so we can measure noisy-neighbor risk and tail behavior):
- 2-week Dedicated POC on 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved environment).
- Synthetic burst tests that simulate 2.5x peak traffic for 48 hours, plus a 72-hour soak at expected peak.
- Noisy-neighbor simulation: run concurrent heavy-generation jobs (long-form summarization) to see tail impact on short prompt latencies.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 token latencies, GPU utilization, queue length, KV cache hit rate, per-tenant token accounting, and audit log retention.

Attachments: SLO matrix (slo_matrix_v2.xlsx), ClearPath requirements (clearpath_requirements_v1.pdf), Redwood Dedicated options (dedicated_capacity_options.pdf).

Next steps (proposed):
- Alex / Patricia: confirm the answers above + whether ClearPath requires single-tenant for production.
- If yes, we can present a Private/VPC and Dedicated comparison with cost/time estimates. If Dedicated is acceptable, we can schedule a POC kickoff week of Oct 12.
- Patricia: please share your procurement contact and any required vendor paperwork.

Thanks — I’ll hold a 30-min slot on Oct 5 and Oct 6 for a short technical pre-POC if helpful.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: [clearpath_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf), slo_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx), dedicated_capacity_options.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alex Rivera <alex@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Patricia Miller <pmiller@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify infra tolerances & isolation expectations for ClearPath POC

Thanks, Tessa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- p95 < 250ms is effectively a hard requirement for any interaction that happens in the clinician UI. p99 can spike higher during rare load events but should ideally be < 800ms. If the p99 is consistently > 800ms under normal peak conditions, that will be a blocker.
- For production we require strict tenant isolation for any workload that processes PHI. We can evaluate Dedicated for POC but if Dedicated implies shared host-level resources that can co-mingle memory/GPU time across tenants we will need Private VPC or an on-prem option for GA.
- Failover: we can tolerate a degraded UX with queued requests, but we cannot have PHI routed outside of cleared environments. So automatic fallback to Hosted is only acceptable for non-PHI traffic.

Procurement notes: Patricia will pick up vendor onboarding — Patricia, I’ve included you here. We’ll need SOC 2 Type II evidence, network diagram (subnet/CIDR), and a template SLA for review.

A quick technical question: would Redwood’s prefix/KV caching help for many of our repeated small prompts? That could reduce GPU load and lower p95.

If Dedicated POC is the lowest-friction path to get meaningful tail-latency data, we’re open to the 2-week plan. Confirming our internal availability for Oct 12 kickoff.

— Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify infra tolerances & isolation expectations for ClearPath POC

Alex / Patricia — looping in procurement info and a quick sketch of commercial options so you have context.

Commercial sketch (ballpark numbers to inform procurement):
- Dedicated (2x A100 reserved pool): ~$32,000/month (committed term options reduce rate). Includes tenant-level segregation, per-tenant metrics, and 30-day SLA for uptime.
- Private VPC (managed by Redwood in customer VPC): one-time onboarding fee ~$40k + ~$40k/month infra run rate (higher ops overhead, full network separation and HSM/KMS integration).
- Hosted (shared) API: lowest cost but not acceptable for PHI unless processed in-cleared pipeline.

Procurement next steps: Patricia, if you can share a redlineable PO template and your standard security questionnaire, we’ll get legal involved and send a DocuSign starter. We can also include a limited DocuSign clause that allows a POC to run under a mutual NDA and a short test data handling addendum.

About fallback behavior: we can implement policy-based routing that restricts PHI traffic to Dedicated or Private targets and allows non-PHI traffic to fall back to Hosted. That avoids PHI leaving the cleared environment.

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify infra tolerances & isolation expectations for ClearPath POC

Alex / team — quick technical follow-up and concrete POC plan so we can get to an engineering kickoff quickly.

Suggested POC plan (detailed):
1) Environment: Dedicated reserved pool (2x A100-equivalent GPUs) for 14 days. We will configure tenant isolation at the job-scheduler level and enable per-process cgroups to reduce cross-job interference.
2) Tests to run:
   - Baseline: 24h run at expected peak (1k RPM) with production-like prompts. Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.
   - Burst: 48h run with bursts at 2.5x peak for 10-minute windows every hour to stress queues and measure tail behavior.
   - Noisy-neighbor sim: launch concurrent long-generation jobs (10–20s jobs) targeting a separate tenant to emulate real-world contention.
   - Recovery: measure time-to-stable p95 after burst ends.
3) Observability we will deliver: per-request tracing (trace id), end-to-end latency breakdown (network, queuing, generation), GPU kernel utilization, and model-variant fallback counts.
4) Data handling: we will treat any payload flagged as PHI as in-scope for Dedicated/Private. Non-PHI traffic may be routed to Hosted for cost effectiveness. We’ll provide an audit log export (CSV) covering token accounting and request headers for the POC window.

Pre-POC checklist (what we need from ClearPath):
- Sanitized sample dataset (or a small synthetic set that matches token distribution).
- Confirmation that PHI flags are available at request time or a list of endpoints that must be PHI-only.
- Network peering details if you want Private VPC testing (CIDR ranges, firewall IPs).

Next steps: if we agree, we’ll prepare the POC runbook and schedule kickoff on Oct 12. I’ve attached the Dedicated options PDF. Tessa / Ben will coordinate contract/PO.

If that date works, say yes and we’ll lock the slot.

— Logan
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
